thread.title: Apple's ills have some analysts worried for Best Buy

author: Mark Reilly
title: Apple's ills have some analysts worried for Best Buy
text: – Managing Editor, Minneapolis / St. Paul Business Journal Jan 4, 2019, 11:00am HST Best Buy Co. Inc. is arguably the biggest seller of Apple Inc. products apart from Apple itself. So what does that mean for the electronics retailer if Apple sales slip? More people are asking that question after the surprise warning by Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) that holiday quarter sales could come in well below estimates; the company cited slow iPhone sales in China. Shares of Apple fell 10 percent on Thursday, helping drag down any companies related to iPhone production or tech as a whole. Some analysts are worried that Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) could also see fallout from Apple's stumbles. CNBC reports how UBS analyst Michael Lasser laid out the stakes for the Richfield-based retailer , noting that an estimated 15 to 20 percent of Best Buy's sales are tied to Apple products, and those generally command higher prices than rival electronics. Best Buy has seen shocks from its Apple relationship before. A holdup in a 2017 iPhone launch left the retailer without a crucial gadget to lure in shoppers, hurting sales. And its shares fell last year when Apple announced a deal to sell products through Best Buy archrival Amazon.com Inc. However, not everybody's worried about Best Buy. Barron's notes that Piper Jaffray kept its $81 target on the stock Thursday , telling investors that "the overall read-thru to Best Buy [from the Apple news] looks neutral." One chief reason not to worry too much: Apple's biggest problems are slow sales in China, and Best Buy has largely exited that market . Shares of Best Buy were down 2 percent Thursday, to $52.10; the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 2.8 percent. – Managing Editor, Minneapolis / St. Paul Business Journal Jan 4, 2019, 11:00am HST Related Content
